discriminator: Ask if any element is an unconventional shape. Runway breaks the grammar once and leaves the rest empty; idol stage keeps every convention and raises the volume of all of them
photographs_as: Wants hard, direct, controlled light so the paint edge stays crisp; soft light turns a graphic into a smudge
use_when: Brand statement, launch key visual, fashion collaboration, art direction that needs to be talked about
avoid_when: Performance advertising and conversion work; a device that stops the scroll can also stop the sale

skin_finish: Genuinely wet — gel, glycerin or water on the skin, with real droplets and real specular points
coverage_texture: Minimal to none; the water is the finish and it has to sit on skin, not on foundation
brows: Slicked, sometimes with gel visible, following the wet logic

liner_lashes: Bare or wet-clumped on purpose; separation is not the goal here
cheeks: Bare or a stain that survives water
contour_highlight: None applied. The water supplies every highlight

signature_tell: Individual droplets with their own tiny highlights, and product that has visibly moved
discriminator: Look for discrete droplets and for pigment that has run. Mul-gwang is a dry-to-touch sheen; wet editorial is actually wet
photographs_as: Needs a hard small source or the droplets lose their highlights and read as blotchy skin

avoid_when: Long-wear, transfer-proof or oil-control claims, which the frame contradicts

skin_finish: One consistent finish across the whole face, chosen to let the single hue read

brows: Often tinted into the hue family, or blocked out entirely
eyeshadow: The hue, on the lid and into the socket
liner_lashes: The hue again, if liner is used at all
cheeks: The hue, placed conventionally

lips: The hue once more, at a different texture — matte lip against a shimmer lid, or the reverse

name_vi: Cô dâu Nam Á cổ điển

origin: Contemporary beauty editorial correcting a documented industry failure
skin_finish: Luminous, with the sheen placed where the bone is and nowhere flat, because deep skin shows a badly placed highlight instantly
coverage_texture: Sheer to medium in a shade matched by undertone rather than by depth; an ashy or grey cast means the undertone is wrong, not the depth
brows: Defined to taste; the register is set by the eye and lip
eyeshadow: Saturated pigment, because sheer washes disappear entirely — jewel tones, metallics and true brights all read where pastels do not
liner_lashes: High-contrast liner if used; a mid-brown liner vanishes
cheeks: Berry, brick, terracotta or true red at genuine saturation; a pale pink turns chalky
contour_highlight: Contour in a warm deeper tone, never grey; highlight in gold or copper, never a cool pearl, which reads as ash
lips: Full saturation in any hue; deep skin carries a true red and a bright orange that lighter skin cannot
palette_retouch: Protect the undertone above all. Do not lighten, do not desaturate the skin, do not lift the shadows into grey
signature_tell: Nothing about the look is a style — it is the same grammar executed with pigment loads and undertones that actually work
discriminator: Not a rival look. This row exists because soft glam executed with default products fails on deep skin, and the failure gets blamed on the model
photographs_as: Needs more exposure latitude and often a second fill; metering for a mid-tone underexposes deep skin, which is the most common technical fault in beauty photography
use_when: Any campaign with deep-skin subjects, which should be most of them
avoid_when: Never avoid. The row to skip is the one that pretends a default palette is universal
source: Recall, unverified 2026-07-30; the underexposure and grey-contour failures are widely documented — check Nyome and Fenty-era coverage plus a working artist

name_vi: Trang điểm hợp khí hậu ẩm
origin: Practical adaptation across Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines
skin_finish: Satin, set on the T-zone, with glow placed as product on the cheekbone rather than as a general dew
coverage_texture: Light to medium, thin layers, because a heavy base slides within an hour
brows: Waterproof and defined; a pencil brow is the first thing humidity removes
eyeshadow: Cream or gel that grips, or powder over a primer; loose glitter is a mistake here
liner_lashes: Waterproof and tubing formulas assumed; tightline rather than a wing, which smudges into the crease
cheeks: Cream under powder so the colour survives a sweat
contour_highlight: Light, cream-based; powder contour in humidity streaks
lips: Tint or stain rather than lipstick, so it survives eating and heat
palette_retouch: Warm, mid contrast; retouch expects visible sheen and should not flatten it
signature_tell: Every formula choice is driven by 80% humidity, and the look is designed to fail gracefully
discriminator: Mul-gwang wants the base wet everywhere; this sets the T-zone flat and places glow only on bone, because in this climate an all-over dew becomes shine within the hour
photographs_as: Honest in daylight; expect to shoot early and to retouch actual sweat rather than pretend it away
use_when: Vietnamese and regional shoots, outdoor location work, long-wear and sunscreen claims
avoid_when: Studio-controlled dewy beauty where the humidity constraint does not apply
source: Recall, unverified 2026-07-30; assembled from regional practice and climate constraints, not from a published standard

eyeshadow: Bronze or copper wash on the lid, nothing in the crease

cheeks: Warm coral or terracotta over the bronzer, placed high
contour_highlight: Bronzer used as both, following where sun would actually fall — temple, cheekbone, jaw, nose bridge
lips: Warm nude, caramel or peach, gloss or balm
palette_retouch: Warm, mid contrast; faux freckles kept in retouch if present

discriminator: Bronzed places warmth where sun lands and leaves the eye simple; latte builds a full brown-toned eye and lip as a colour story rather than as a tan
photographs_as: Suits hard directional light and a warm grade; cool grades turn bronzer orange
use_when: Sun care, self-tan, summer, swim, holiday campaigns
avoid_when: Brightening and whitening claims, and any market where tanned skin carries the wrong class coding — check locally

name_vi: Tránh bệt trắng khi chụp flash
origin: A photographic failure mode, not a style
skin_finish: Any finish, provided the products carry no light-scattering mineral filter where flash will hit
coverage_texture: Any coverage, but every product in the base has to be checked, not just the foundation
brows: Unaffected
eyeshadow: Unaffected
liner_lashes: Unaffected
cheeks: Unaffected
contour_highlight: Setting powder is the usual culprit; a translucent powder heavy in titanium dioxide or zinc oxide is the single most common cause
lips: Unaffected
palette_retouch: A grey-white cast on the T-zone that no grade fixes cleanly; this has to be prevented on set
signature_tell: The face photographs grey-white and lighter than the neck under flash, while looking correct to the eye
discriminator: Not a look at all. If a face reads white under flash and normal in daylight, it is flashback; if it reads white in both, it is intentional
photographs_as: The whole point. Test with the actual flash before the subject is in wardrobe, not after
use_when: Any shoot using flash — event, bridal, PR, red carpet, press
avoid_when: Never skip. Also check SPF in the base, which causes the same cast

name_vi: Chụp swatch cho thương mại điện tử
skin_finish: Bare skin only, matte, on the arm or the lip; a base under a swatch changes the colour
coverage_texture: None. Any coverage under the swatch invalidates it
brows: Not in frame
eyeshadow: Swatched as drawn-down stripes of even thickness with visible gaps, on bare skin, in one pass
liner_lashes: Swatched as a drawn line at product width, not smudged
cheeks: Swatched both sheer and built up, so the buyer sees the range rather than one point
contour_highlight: Not applicable
lips: Applied full-opacity to a bare lip with no liner and no gloss, since both shift the shade
palette_retouch: Colour accuracy above everything. Grey-card the shot and do not adjust saturation. A retouched swatch is a returns problem and, if it misstates the shade, a claims problem
signature_tell: Bare skin, even stripes, one light, a grey card in the first frame
discriminator: A swatch proves what the colour is; a before-and-after proves what a product did. Different claims, different evidence, and they are not interchangeable
photographs_as: One consistent light and one white balance across the whole range, or shades cannot be compared to each other
use_when: Product listings, shade ranges, palette launches, marketplace assets
avoid_when: As a beauty asset. A swatch is evidence, not a mood
source: Recall, unverified 2026-07-30; marketplace image requirements are published by each platform — read the live spec rather than this row

origin: An advertising-compliance constraint expressed as a makeup and lighting brief
skin_finish: The before and the after must differ only by the product. Same finish logic, same skin prep otherwise
coverage_texture: If the after adds base coverage, the frame proves coverage and nothing else
brows: Identical in both, or the pair is not comparable
eyeshadow: Identical in both unless the eye product is the subject
liner_lashes: For a mascara or lash claim, the before must be genuinely bare — no curler, no clear coat, no fibre
cheeks: Identical in both
contour_highlight: Identical in both. A highlight added only to the after is the most common way these frames cheat
lips: Identical in both unless the lip product is the subject
palette_retouch: Same crop, same distance, same lens, same light, same exposure, same grade, same retouch level. Log all eight, because a regulator will ask
signature_tell: Only one variable changes between the two frames, and the change is the product
discriminator: A before-and-after asserts causation and needs the pair controlled; a swatch asserts only colour. Confusing them produces an unsupportable claim
photographs_as: Shoot the before and the after in the same session under a locked setup; never reconstruct a before afterwards
use_when: Efficacy claims, skincare, treatment, clinic, lash and brow services
avoid_when: Whenever the pair cannot be controlled. Then it is not evidence and the claim has to be dropped. Log it in the claims ledger either way

origin: Western social and editorial beauty, 2018 onward
skin_finish: Sheer and satin, because a freckle drawn on a full base reads as a dot on paint
coverage_texture: Sheer, so real texture supports the drawn marks
brows: Soft, brushed
eyeshadow: Minimal
liner_lashes: Minimal
cheeks: Cream, under or over the freckles depending on how sunken they should read
contour_highlight: Light bronzer following a sun path, since freckles imply sun
lips: Balm or tint
palette_retouch: Warm, mid contrast; keep the freckles varied in size and density in retouch
signature_tell: Marks cluster where sun lands — nose bridge and upper cheek — at irregular sizes, and thin out toward the jaw
discriminator: Freckles are discrete marks; bronzing is a continuous wash. They pair well, and evenly spaced same-size dots are how a faked freckle gives itself away
photographs_as: Wants soft daylight; hard light makes the drawn marks look like dirt
use_when: Youth, natural positioning, sun care, tint launches
avoid_when: Skincare treating pigmentation, where drawing on the thing the product removes is incoherent

skin_finish: Any; the liner is the device
coverage_texture: Medium, even, so the wing has a clean ground
brows: Defined with a lifted tail, echoing the wing
eyeshadow: Neutral, or a soft outer-corner deepening; the lid stays quiet under the liner
liner_lashes: Liner thin at the inner corner, thickening through the outer third, then flicked up and out past the corner at a clear angle; lashes weighted outward
cheeks: Cheekbone, medium, blended toward the ear
contour_highlight: Light; a highlight under the wing's tail sharpens it
lips: Free. A nude keeps the eye dominant, a red makes the pair the whole look
palette_retouch: Neutral to warm, mid to high contrast, the wing edge kept crisp
signature_tell: Liner is thickest in the outer third and leaves the eye entirely, flicking upward
discriminator: The angle of the exit. A cat eye flicks up; a siren eye extends nearly horizontally and empties the inner corner, which the cat eye does not bother to do
photographs_as: Reads at any size and under most light, which is why it has never gone away
use_when: Liner launches, classic and confident registers, anything that needs one legible device
avoid_when: Cute and youth positioning, and any frame where the eye will be closed or downcast

skin_finish: Satin, dewy on the cheekbone
coverage_texture: Light, with the under-eye left uncorrected so the pink reads
brows: Soft straight, low contrast
eyeshadow: Pink or coral washed onto the lid, the inner corner and the lower lash line, plus a wet-look gloss or pearl on the centre lid so the eye looks glazed
liner_lashes: Tightline only; the lower waterline brightened rather than lined, lashes softly clumped at the inner corner
cheeks: Pink drawn up onto the under-eye and across the nose bridge
contour_highlight: Pearl on the inner corner, the nose tip and the cupid's bow — the three places a real tear would catch light
lips: Pink tint, glossy, blurred
palette_retouch: Cool pink, low contrast, high-key; the glaze must survive retouch
signature_tell: A glazed wet lid over pink under-eye and nose, so the face reads as if it has just stopped crying
discriminator: The lid. Crying eye glazes it wet and brightens the waterline; under-eye blush leaves the lid dry and does nothing to the waterline
photographs_as: Needs a small hard source to make the glaze catch; under flat light it reads as an unfinished face
use_when: Youth, K-beauty, gloss and blush launches, emotive storytelling
avoid_when: Authority, clinical, corporate, and markets where the reference reads as distressing rather than sweet

origin: Asian-American subculture, California 2010s; revived and softened on TikTok early 2020s
skin_finish: Matte to satin, bronzed a step deeper than the neck admits
coverage_texture: Full and sculpted; the tan is part of the look, not a correction
brows: Straight to soft arch, filled solid, squared front, crisp tail
eyeshadow: Bronze and copper smoked outward, shimmer or glitter on the centre lid
liner_lashes: Sharp elongated black wing, tightlined; dramatic wispy strip lashes long enough to read at arm's length
cheeks: Bronzer-led; blush minimal, warmth comes from contour
contour_highlight: Heavy visible contour, nose sculpted, cheekbone cut; golden highlight on the high points
lips: Overlined matte nude-brown or mauve, ombre toward the centre acceptable
palette_retouch: Warm bronzed grade, high contrast, sharpened
signature_tell: The wing and the brow carry the look: hard black elongated liner over bronzed monochrome warmth, straight brow, nude-brown lip
discriminator: Both are heavy glam. ABG runs bronzed-monochrome with a harder longer wing, straighter brow and nude-brown lip; Instagram glam runs cut-crease colour, arched brow and a concealer-bright under-eye
photographs_as: Reads at phone distance and in club or neon light; soft daylight exposes the lash band and contour edges
use_when: Streetwear, nail-lash-brow studios, boba and nightlife brands, diaspora-adjacent fashion social; pairs with pin-straight hair and money pieces
avoid_when: Bridal, corporate, skincare-truth briefs, any brand claiming barefaced natural
source: Recall, unverified 2026-08-07; check current TikTok and Instagram ABG creators — the look has softened toward clean-girl hybrids since 2022
